title: Which Masai Mara Safari Package Fits Your Holiday? Road, Fly-in and Conservancy Trips Compared
meta_title: Masai Mara Safari Packages Compared, With Prices in £
meta_description: Masai Mara safari packages compared: road, fly-in and conservancy trips, what they include and prices in pounds and dollars for UK travellers.
excerpt: Masai Mara safari packages explained for UK travellers: the three main package types, what each includes, starting prices in pounds and dollars, and the questions to ask before paying a deposit.
content:
Masai Mara safari packages bundle your vehicle, guide, park fees, meals and camp into one price, and they come in three main types: road trips from Nairobi, fly-in trips from Wilson Airport and conservancy stays. From the UK, most travellers book three to five days in the Mara as part of a week-long holiday.

The hard part is comparing Masai Mara safari packages from different sellers. One price includes flights to the airstrip and another does not, one lists the reserve fee and another hides it, and most quote in US dollars. This guide explains what each package type includes, what it costs in pounds and dollars, and how to read a quote before you pay a deposit. For the wider picture, start with our Kenya safari packages.

Quick Facts

  • Package types: road safari from Nairobi, fly-in safari, conservancy safari
  • Typical length: 2-4 nights in the Mara, often inside a 7-10 day Kenya holiday
  • Reserve fee: US$100 per adult per day January-June, US$200 July-December (checked November 2026)
  • Getting there: about 5 hours by road from Nairobi, or a light-aircraft flight from Wilson Airport
  • From the UK: nonstop Heathrow-Nairobi flights take about 9 hours (checked November 2026)
  • Exchange rate used: £1 = US$1.31 (indicative mid-market rate, 25 November 2026)

What Are Masai Mara Safari Packages?

Masai Mara safari packages are pre-planned trips that combine transport, accommodation, park fees, meals and game drives in the Masai Mara for one per-person price. A good package also names the camp, the vehicle type and exactly which nights you spend where.

In the UK, a package usually means flights plus hotel. On safari it usually means the ground arrangements only. Your international flight to Nairobi is booked separately, and the safari starts when your guide meets you at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport or your Nairobi hotel.

Most Masai Mara safari packages are private, meaning the vehicle is yours for the trip. Budget trips may use a shared vehicle, which is cheaper but less flexible, so ask which one you are being quoted.

Which Type of Mara Package Suits Your Holiday?

The right choice among Masai Mara safari packages depends on how many days you have and how you feel about long drives. Road trips suit travellers with a week or more who want to see Lake Nakuru or Naivasha too, fly-in trips suit short holidays, and conservancy trips suit those who want walks, night drives and fewer vehicles.

Package typeHow you travelBest forWatch out for
Road safari4x4 Land Cruiser with pop-up roof, about 5 hours each way from NairobiLonger holidays, families, adding lakes en routeTwo long travel days; rough final stretch of road
Fly-in safariScheduled light aircraft from Wilson Airport to a Mara airstripShort holidays, honeymoons, safari plus beach15 kg soft-bag limit; flight cost per person
Conservancy safariUsually fly-in, staying in a private conservancy next to the reserveWalking, night drives, quieter sightingsHigher nightly rates; reserve visits may cost extra
Budget camping or tentedShared or private vehicle, simple camps near a reserve gateTight budgets, younger travellersBasic rooms; shared vehicle timings

Road Masai Mara safari packages

The road option is the classic Kenya safari. Our 4-day Naivasha, Nakuru and Masai Mara safari covers Hell's Gate, a Lake Naivasha boat ride and a night at Lake Nakuru, then a drive of about five hours to two nights in the Mara.

Fly-in and conservancy packages

Fly-in Masai Mara safari packages save around ten hours on the road over a round trip. Our 4-day Masai Mara flight safari includes return scheduled flights from Wilson Airport, airstrip transfers and three nights in a tented camp. Excess baggage over the light-aircraft limit, usually 15 kg in soft bags, is not included, so pack a duffel instead of a hard suitcase.

Conservancy-based Masai Mara safari packages stay in the private areas around the reserve, such as Mara Naboisho,, where camps limit vehicles and offer walks and night drives the main reserve does not allow. They cost more per night, but sightings are quieter. Read our guide to the Masai Mara reserve versus conservancies before choosing.

How Much Do Masai Mara Safari Packages Cost in Pounds?

Masai Mara safari packages start at about £670 per adult for four days in simple tented camps and run past £2,000 for a week with good lodges in migration season. Prices below are Divulge starting prices in US dollars, converted at £1 = US$1.31, the indicative rate on 25 November 2026.

7-day Mara river crossing safariUS$2,850£2,180Amboseli, Nakuru and 3 Mara nights, 4-star stays

Most Masai Mara safari packages are priced in US dollars because park fees and many camps are set in dollars. Your card provider or bank will add its own margin when you pay, so the final sterling figure is usually a little higher than the mid-market conversion.

Why the same Masai Mara safari packages cost more from July

The Masai Mara reserve fee for non-resident adults is US$100 per day from January to June and US$200 from July to December, about £76 and £153; children aged 9-17 pay US$50 and under-8s are free (checked November 2026, Mara Triangle conservation fees). On a three-night stay, that alone adds about £230 per adult in the second half of the year. Our Masai Mara safari cost guide breaks down every line.

What Should a Masai Mara Package Include?

Complete Masai Mara safari packages should include the vehicle and guide, all park and conservancy fees, accommodation on full board, game drives and drinking water. If any of these is missing, the low headline price will rise once you add them back, so ask for an itemised includes and excludes list.

ItemUsually includedUsually extra
Transport4x4 vehicle and driver guide; light-aircraft flights on fly-in tripsExcess baggage over 15 kg
FeesReserve or conservancy fees for the nights bookedDay visits to the main reserve from some conservancies
Food and drinkBreakfast, lunch and dinner; drinking water on drivesAlcohol, soft drinks, laundry
ActivitiesGame drives as per the itineraryBalloon flight (US$480 per person on our trips), village visit on some trips
TravelAirport or hotel pick-up in NairobiInternational flights, eTA, travel insurance
TipsNever includedAbout US$10 per person per day suggested for the guide

Four questions to ask before paying a deposit

First, is the vehicle private or shared? Second, which camp is confirmed, and what does "or similar" mean? Third, do the fees cover every Mara day, including travel days? Fourth, what are the payment and cancellation terms? Get all four answers in writing.

Check also whether Masai Mara safari packages are priced per person sharing a room. Solo travellers usually pay a single supplement, and families should ask about child rates. Our Masai Mara camps by budget guide helps you judge a named camp.

How Do You Get to the Masai Mara From the UK?

Travellers from the UK fly into Nairobi first, then reach the Mara by road or light aircraft. Nonstop flights from London Heathrow to Nairobi with British Airways and Kenya Airways take about 9 hours (route schedules checked November 2026), and Kenya is three hours ahead of GMT.

Overnight flights from Heathrow usually land in Nairobi in the morning. Fly-in trips then transfer across the city to Wilson Airport, so allow time between flights.

From regional UK airports, and from Ireland, Australia and New Zealand, routes to Nairobi normally connect through a European or Gulf hub. Book the international flight first, then fit your Masai Mara safari packages around it.

Entry, health and safety checks for British travellers

British passport holders need a Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation, applied for online through the official Kenya eTA site, and the FCDO recommends applying at least two weeks before you travel (FCDO Kenya entry requirements, checked November 2026). Our Kenya eTA guide walks through the form.

UK travel health guidance rates malaria risk as high in safari areas, including the Masai Mara, so speak to your GP or a travel clinic about tablets several weeks before you go (TravelHealthPro Kenya, checked November 2026). The FCDO travel advice for Kenya advises against travel to some areas near the Somali border, far from the Mara; read the current version before booking.

When Is the Best Time to Book Masai Mara Safari Packages?

The best time for Masai Mara safari packages depends on what you want to see. July to October brings the wildebeest migration and the highest prices, January to March is dry and quieter with lower fees, and April and May are the long rains, when some camps close and others offer their lowest rates.

UK holiday windowMara conditionsBooking advice
February half-termDry season, resident wildlife, lower reserve feeGood value; book 3-4 months ahead
Summer holidays (late July-August)Migration herds usually in the MaraBook 6-9 months ahead for named camps
October half-termHerds often still present, short rains may beginFewer families; good for couples
Christmas and New YearGreen, warm, peak festive ratesBook early; flights fill fast

The herds move with the rain, so no month is guaranteed. Our Great Migration month by month guide shows where they usually are, and the best time to visit the Masai Mara covers the rest of the year.

Insider Tips

  • Fly in, drive out: one light-aircraft leg saves a long travel day without paying for two flights.
  • Count full days: a 3-day package often means one full day in the Mara; four days gives two.
  • Pay in dollars smartly: use a card without foreign transaction fees to keep the sterling cost close to the quote.
  • Ask about June: the lower reserve fee runs until 30 June, and the first herds can arrive in some years.
  • Insure early: buy travel insurance when you pay the deposit, not just before you fly.

How Many Days Should Your Mara Package Be?

For Masai Mara safari packages, three or four nights is the sweet spot for most UK travellers. That gives two or three full days of drives and a buffer if rain costs you one.

Two-night trips suit a Mara add-on from the coast, such as our 2-day Masai Mara safari from Diani, but feel rushed on their own. With a week, add Amboseli or the Rift Valley lakes. Our 7-day Kenya safari itinerary shows how the days fit together.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is included in Masai Mara safari packages?

Masai Mara safari packages from a Nairobi operator normally include the vehicle, driver guide, park fees, full-board meals, accommodation and drinking water. Fly-in versions add the light-aircraft flights from Wilson Airport. International flights, the Kenya eTA, travel insurance, tips, drinks and the balloon flight are usually extra, so check the excludes list.

How much are Masai Mara safari packages in pounds?

Masai Mara safari packages on our site start at about £670 per adult for four days in simple camps with a shared vehicle, converted from US$880 at the 25 November 2026 rate. Private road trips with lodges start around £1,245 for four days, and a seven-day migration trip from about £2,180, before flights from the UK.

Is it better to fly or drive to the Masai Mara?

Flying to the Masai Mara is a short light-aircraft hop from Wilson Airport that saves around ten hours of driving on a return trip, which suits short holidays. Driving takes about five hours each way, costs less and lets you add Lake Nakuru or Naivasha. Flying in and driving out balances time and budget for many travellers from the UK.

How many days do I need in the Masai Mara?

Most travellers need two or three full days in the Masai Mara to see the reserve properly, which means three or four nights on the ground. Two-day trips work as an add-on to a beach holiday but leave little margin for bad weather or a quiet morning. In migration months, an extra day raises your chance of seeing a river crossing.

When should I book a Masai Mara safari from the UK?

Book a Masai Mara safari for July to October, or for Christmas, six to nine months ahead if you want a specific camp, because migration rooms and school-holiday flights from London fill first. For January to June you can often book two to three months out, and reserve fees are lower in that half of the year.

Final Thoughts

The best Masai Mara safari packages are the ones whose price you can read line by line: named camp, private or shared vehicle, every park day covered and a clear list of extras. Choose road, fly-in or conservancy by your holiday length, then book around the UK school calendar.
